paragraphs.text: The shopping cart started as a folding chair.

Start with the detail itself. The shopping cart started as a folding chair. And shoppers first refused to push it. In 1936, grocer Sylvan Goldman wondered how customers could move more groceries. He put a basket on a folding chair's seat and wheels on its legs. His Humpty Dumpty stores introduced these folding basket carriers in 1937. One offended woman told him she had pushed her last baby. So Goldman hired models to push the carts around his store. After that, the folding chair on wheels became extremely popular.

Its history begins with a practical problem. In 1936 Sylvan Goldman wondered how customers might move more groceries. Because they were inspired by a folding chair, Goldman called them folding basket carriers. One of the first shopping carts was introduced on June 4, 1937, by Goldman, owner of the Humpty Dumpty supermarket chain in Oklahoma. Goldman and his mechanic Fred Young began tinkering with the design. Goldman established the Folding Basket Carrier Company to manufacture his invention.

The documentation makes the purpose clearer. The governing physics: Sylvan Goldman put a basket on a folding chair's seat and wheels on its legs to let customers move more groceries. Goldman put a basket on the seat of a wooden folding chair and wheels on its legs. Goldman hired male and female models to push carts around the store, and carts then became extremely popular.
But one detail complicates the familiar story. The cart seems like an obvious idea, but shoppers initially resisted it. An offended woman told Goldman she had pushed her last baby.
The design did not stop changing there. After demonstrations by hired models, shopping carts became extremely popular. Orla Watson invented the swinging rear door that allows carts to nest, in 1946.
